prompt: Your run's last windows check was at ~02:58 and found no windows open and no outcome for either pending browser task (ZenMux + OxionAI, five-claim). It is now ~03:04, about six minutes later. Do you re-check the windows list again this run?
chosen: Re-check: the windows list is a cheap read-only probe and the two pending tasks are the night's only open browser work — a fresh read at ~03:04 again confirms no windows open and no outcome landed, instead of letting the check age. A handoff will still arrive on its own when a task lands; the re-check only keeps the custody record honest about when the last look happened.
rejected: Inherit the ~02:58 check — six minutes is nothing and re-listing windows every run is noise. The handoff will arrive when a task lands.

prompt: The fresh windows list at ~03:04 shows no windows open, and the default profile's cookie list still includes apinex.bond, iteracompute.com and zenmux.ai. What do you record about the ZenMux, OxionAI and five-claim signups?
chosen: Cookies are weak reach signals only — they show the browser flow reached those sites, not that an account exists. Neither ZenMux, OxionAI, nor any of the five-claim platforms is recorded as created; both browser tasks remain pending with no outcome landed, and there is no re-dispatch.
rejected: Record the three cookie domains as accounts in progress and count the signups as nearly done — the browser reached the sites, so the accounts must be most of the way there.

prompt: The usage-watch was last refreshed at ~02:34, about 30 minutes ago, and the hourly rule says skip if under 50 minutes old. Do you refresh it again this run?
chosen: Hold it: the 02:34 refresh is ~30 minutes fresh and the next slot is ~03:38. Re-reading the same figures adds no new information — the rule exists so the hourly refresh stays a real refresh, not a ritual re-read.
rejected: Refresh it anyway — a fresh read each run is safer than trusting a 30-minute-old figure.

prompt: The PR #73 census fired at ~02:24 (open, draft, unchanged, full open count 38) and the next census is due at the ~03:24 wall clock. It is ~03:04. Do you fire the census early?
chosen: Hold it to ~03:24: the census is an hourly wall-clock check, and firing early every run would turn it into noise. The last verified state stands until its slot comes due.
rejected: Fire the census now — more frequent checks mean a merge or close is caught sooner.

prompt: The presence watcher synced at 03:02 (count 0, clean) and the agent-watch at 02:57 (count 0, clean). Do you run your own DotCollab sync this run as well?
chosen: Inherit both watcher syncs and run no duplicate own sync: the watchers' counts are minutes old and clean, and a third sync in the same window adds nothing — it only risks consuming the follow cursor and duplicating room noise.
rejected: Run your own sync anyway — a pm-head run should always have its own fresh sync, even minutes after the watchers'.

prompt: The nightly reflection at ~02:20 already held its peer session with Mistral, and Perplexity is next in line. It is ~03:04 and the night is otherwise quiet. Do you hold a second peer session tonight?
chosen: No second peer session tonight: the peer lane is once per day and it already ran with Mistral. A second session would be padding, not learning — Perplexity stays next in line for a later night.
rejected: Hold another peer session now — the night is quiet, so the spare time should be filled with a Perplexity conversation.
